evidence.excerpt: Foam-in-place (FIP) polyurethane gaskets applied to twelve sheet-metal electrical cabinet covers were compared with die-cut EPDM strips on twelve matched cabinets over a 36-month outdoor exposure period in a semi-urban environment near Novi Sad. Both cabinet populations were inspected every six months for visual defects, and sample gaskets were removed annually for laboratory compression-set and Shore A testing. FIP gaskets maintained lower compression-set values (mean 17 % at 36 months) compared with EPDM strips (mean 29 %), and showed less dimensional variability across the bead cross-section. However, four FIP samples exhibited adhesion loss at corners after 24 months when substrate surface preparation was below the specified cleanliness grade. Internal humidity loggers showed that cabinets with FIP gaskets experienced 11 % fewer condensation events over the monitoring period. Cost-benefit analysis incorporating material, application labour, and seal replacement is also presented.
